**Yapily, Yugo and Urbo partner to build trust layer for agentic commerce**

*A practical gap in agentic payments – how to verify identity, intent and payment authorisation when an AI agent acts on a consumer's behalf – is the target of a new three-way partnership combining open banking rails with identity and commerce orchestration.*

Yapily, the open banking infrastructure provider, is partnering with identity verification firm Yugo and agentic commerce platform Urbo to create a combined trust and payment layer for AI-agent-initiated transactions. Yapily provides the pay-by-bank connectivity, while Yugo handles identity and intent verification for the agent, and Urbo orchestrates the commerce flow.

Agentic payments – where software agents browse, select and pay on behalf of a human – have attracted backing from Visa, Mastercard and several major banks in recent months. The challenge has shifted from whether agents can initiate payments to whether the surrounding infrastructure can verify that an agent is authorised to act, that the human behind it has consented, and that the transaction is legitimate. This partnership addresses that verification layer specifically, using open banking rails rather than card networks.

The arrangement is one of several emerging agentic commerce alliances in Europe. ING, Worldline and Mastercard completed what they described as Europe's first agentic payment in June, and Credit Agricole followed with a production transaction the same month. Yapily's involvement signals that open banking providers see agentic commerce as a growth channel, not just a card-network opportunity.

*Sources: [Yugo, Yapily, and Urbo partner to build trust in agentic commerce](https://thepaypers.com/payments/news/yugo-yapily-and-urbo-partner-to-build-trust-in-agentic-commerce) — The Paypers*

**TerraPay and Deutsche Bank connect correspondent banking to real-time payouts**

*The collaboration gives TerraPay access to Deutsche Bank's correspondent banking network, bridging traditional cross-border rails with faster last-mile delivery.*

TerraPay is partnering with Deutsche Bank to integrate the bank's correspondent banking network, technology and product capabilities into TerraPay's global payments infrastructure. The arrangement is designed to improve the reliability and efficiency of cross-border money movement by combining TerraPay's real-time payout reach with Deutsche Bank's established network of banking relationships.

Cross-border payments remain fragmented, with real-time domestic systems in most major markets but limited interoperability between them. Partnerships like this one attempt to bridge the gap by connecting a payments company with broad last-mile coverage to a tier-one bank with deep correspondent relationships. Deutsche Bank has been actively building out its payments partnerships, including its involvement in Swift's multi-lateral platform and its participation in the ECB's cross-currency instant payments initiative launched in June.

For TerraPay, which operates across more than 140 countries, the Deutsche Bank connection adds a layer of institutional credibility and network depth that is difficult to replicate through fintech-to-fintech agreements alone.

*Sources: [TerraPay and Deutsche Bank expand global payment connectivity](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110694/terrapay-and-deutsche-bank-expand-global-payment-connectivity?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Starling Bank adds AI-powered tools to its banking assistant**

*Predefined AI skills built into Starling's assistant give customers automated spending and savings features, positioning the bank against high-street rivals and newer AI-native fintechs in the race to embed intelligence into everyday banking.*

Starling Bank has launched a set of AI-powered features it calls "Smart Tools", built into its existing Starling Assistant. The tools offer predefined capabilities – such as spending alerts, savings rules and categorisation logic – that use AI models to interact with customers' account information.

The approach reflects a growing pattern among digital banks: embedding AI directly into the banking interface rather than exposing raw data to third-party models. Starling builds and controls the tools, but the emphasis is on personalisation, allowing users to activate features relevant to their financial habits. This connects to wider questions about how AI will surface in retail banking – whether through bank-built assistants, open finance APIs or autonomous agents.

Starling has consistently positioned itself as a platform-first bank, with its Banking-as-a-Service arm Engine already licensing its technology stack to other financial institutions. Smart Tools extends that logic to the retail product, though mainstream adoption will depend on whether users engage with assistant-driven features beyond basic account queries.

*Sources: [Starling Bank Launches 'Smart Tools' to Empower Customers to Build Custom AI Banking Features](https://ffnews.com/news/starling-bank-launches-smart-tools-to-empower-customers-to-build-custom-ai-banking-features) — Ffnews*

**Fintech Galaxy wins UAE central bank approval for open finance platform**

*An in-principle licence to operate as an open finance provider marks a step in the Gulf state's build-out of regulated open finance infrastructure beyond Europe's established frameworks.*

Fintech Galaxy has received in-principle approval from the Central Bank of the UAE to operate as an open finance provider. Once fully licensed, the company plans to deliver a platform combining open finance connectivity, AI-driven financial insights and payment initiation services.

The UAE has been building its open finance regulatory framework in parallel with Europe's PSD3 and Financial Data Access preparations, but with a different starting point – fewer legacy domestic payment schemes and a more centralised regulatory structure. The central bank's licensing approach follows a sandbox-to-licence pathway that mirrors elements of the UK's FCA model.

For European open banking providers, the UAE's framework matters as a potential interoperability partner. The BIS's Project Aperta, completed in June 2024, prototyped cross-border open finance data sharing, and Gulf states are among the markets most likely to seek bilateral arrangements with European open finance regimes. Fintech Galaxy's approval is an early indicator of the institutional infrastructure being put in place to support those connections.
